title: Why You Always Pick the Middle Option

vo.en: You are being tricked into spending more.

visual.description: Close up of a man looking confused while examining a restaurant menu.

vo.en: Ever wonder why you never pick the cheapest coffee, but always shy away from the most expensive one?

visual.description: A man's hands holding coffee cups of different sizes on a wooden table.

vo.en: Companies use a psychological glitch called the decoy effect to manipulate your daily choices.

visual.description: A man pointing at price tags on a display board in a store.

vo.en: They purposely introduce a useless third option that makes the middle choice look like an absolute bargain.

visual.description: A man tapping on a smartphone screen while reviewing subscription plans.

vo.en: Suddenly, your brain anchors to the highest price, making you feel smart for settling on the middle.

visual.description: A man touching his head in realization while working at a desk.

vo.en: Follow, part two drops tomorrow because... you are being tricked into spending more.

visual.description: A man walking away through a busy subway station corridor.
